text:
A: Hello, can you hear me all right? I'm Alison.
B: Yes, perfectly. I'm Abena. Hello.
A: Hello. Oh, I love your shelf. All those books and the little vases. I said that when I saw your picture, she must be ever so well-read.
B: (laughs) Well, I try. Thank you. Some of those vases I bought from a potter in Accra. Where are you?
A: Ipswich. Suffolk. I'm a practice nurse at a GP surgery, so asthma, diabetes, smears, that sort of thing. And you?
B: I'm an interior designer, part-time, for a studio in Dulwich. I'm in Herne Hill, South London.
A: Oh, that sounds lovely. Do you go in people's houses and choose everything?
B: Sort of. I meet clients, listen to what they want, which is often not what they say. Then mood boards, fabrics, furniture. It's two short days a fortnight, so it never becomes a grind.
A: Not what they say, yes, we get that with patients. They come in for a blood pressure check and at the door, it's "oh, while I'm here".
B: (laughs) Exactly that. The real thing comes at the end.
A: It always does. Sorry, I've got a cat who might wander across. Biscuit. He's a menace.
B: That's fine. Erm, do you have family nearby?
A: My son's in Colchester, with his partner and the baby. I have her on Fridays. My daughter's in Bristol. You?
B: A daughter in Manchester, and a son in Peckham, who is very close and never answers his phone.
A: (laughs) Oh, they don't, do they? Mine texts "all good" and that's it.
B: Well, "all good" is more than I get. My mother's the opposite, in Accra. She rings every day. She's getting frail now, so I'm thinking about how much time to spend there.
A: Oh, that's hard. Being so far away. Is she managing on her own?
B: There's family around. But you wonder, you know. Whether you should be there more.
A: Of course you do. My dad had COPD, and towards the end I was round every day, and it still didn't feel like enough. I don't know if that helps at all, sorry.
B: No, it does. Thank you. It's good to hear it from someone who's done it.
A: Do you get back often?
B: Every year or two, usually Christmas. And it's harvest at church soon, so I'm on decorations, which I was just telling someone about.
A: Oh, harvest! I do the food bank collection at ours. We get some funny tins. And I sing in a choir as well, alto, we're starting on the Christmas concert.
B: Oh, lovely. Singing is my favourite part of church, honestly. Ours is a Ghanaian Methodist congregation, so it's loud, with drums.
A: Oh, I'd love that. Ours is very proper. We get told off for breathing in the wrong place.
B: (laughs) You should visit one Sunday. You'd be very welcome. Do you travel at all?
A: Once a year with my sister. We did a river cruise on the Douro, I still talk about it. Porto was beautiful.
B: I love Portugal. Lisbon especially, the tiles. I plan everything around the galleries and the markets —
